description.en: Grammar, vocabulary and skills: reading, writing and speaking.

html.en:
We use the Present Simple for things that are always true or that happen again and again: routines, habits, facts and timetables.
She plays tennis every day. · The sun rises in the east. · The train leaves at 6:45.

rows.en: She plays tennis. · My cat sleeps on the bed.

html.en: Memory trick: He, She, It → HeSIt → they all "hesitate" and add an -s.

rows.en: play → plays · read → reads · run → runs · like → likes
Verbs ending in s, ss, sh, ch, x, o
miss → misses · wash → washes · watch → watches · mix → mixes · go → goes · do → does
cry → cries · fly → flies · study → studies · carry → carries
play → plays · buy → buys · stay → stays · enjoy → enjoys

html.en: The full spelling list from your worksheet: watch–watches · read–reads · cry–cries · dress–dresses · do–does · wash–washes · stay–stays · study–studies · go–goes · run–runs · kiss–kisses · jump–jumps · fly–flies · play–plays · teach–teaches · like–likes · brush–brushes · cook–cooks · buy–buys · mix–mixes

The -s jumps to the helper! Once you use doesn't, the main verb loses its -s.
✗ She doesn't likes pizza. → ✓ She doesn't like pizza.

Do / Does + subject + base verb + …?
Do you like pizza? · Does she read books? · Does your mum cook dinner?
Wh- questions: question word first → What does the sun make? · Where does he live? · When does school start? · How often do you play football?

Subject → Verb → Object → Place → Time
I  ·  watch  ·  TikTok  ·  in my room  ·  before bed.

They go before the main verb but after the verb "be":
She always has cereal. · He never goes out on weekdays. · Wendy is always nervous.
Time expressions (every day, on Mondays, twice a week, in the evening) go at the end.
7️⃣ The 8 mistakes examiners love to find

An indefinite pronoun is a pronoun that refers to a person, a place or a thing without saying exactly who, where or what it is.
I have eaten everything in my fridge. · I need to find something. · Anything would be okay. · I have nothing for breakfast.
-one and -body mean exactly the same thing: someone = somebody, no one = nobody, everyone = everybody. Pick either one.

rows.en: 👤👤👤🙋  — one of them (we don't know which)

html.en:
The 4 rules

  1. They are singular → the verb takes an -s.
    ✓ Everybody needs a friend.   ✗ Everybody need a friend.
    ✓ Is anybody at home?   ✗ Are anybody at home?
  2. some- in + affirmative sentences → I have something. There is somebody outside.
  3. any- in ? questions and − negatives → Do you know anybody here? · I don't have anything.
  4. no- is already negative — never use it with not / don't.
    ✓ I have nothing. = ✓ I don't have anything.   ✗ I don't have nothing.

Some / Any / No — the three-way switch
I have something. → I don't have anything. → I have nothing.
There is somebody. → There is not anybody. → There is nobody.
We will go somewhere. → We will not go anywhere. → We will go nowhere.
Exception: use some- in a question when you offer or ask for something: Would you like something to drink? · Can somebody help me?

rows.en: 1. I looked ______ for my cat, but I couldn't find it.
2. James called his friend, but ______ answered the phone.
3. I didn't go ______ on the weekend, so I was really bored.
4. Let's get ______ to eat after our class.
5. Did you hear that? I think ______ rang the doorbell.
6. ______ was on time. No one was late.
7. I didn't eat ______ for lunch, so I'm really hungry now.

html.en: Notice #11: the adjective goes after the pronoun → somewhere interesting, something new, nothing special.

html.en: A collocation is a pair of words that English speakers always put together. They are not logical — you just have to learn them as one block. You make your bed, you don't "do" your bed.

title.en: 🗂️ 4 · Vocabulary — holidays · free time · home · clothes

html.en:
📖 Reading — how to get every mark

  1. Read the questions first, then the text. You will know what to hunt for.
  2. Read the whole text once without stopping at unknown words.
  3. Underline the part of the text that gives each answer, and write the line number next to the question.
  4. True / False: if any part of the sentence is wrong, the whole answer is False.
  5. Copy names, numbers and spellings exactly from the text.
  6. Answer with a full sentence unless the paper says one word.

✍️ Writing — the 5-step routine

  1. Read the task twice. How many words? What must you include? (Usually 60–80 words and 3 content points.)
  2. Plan for 2 minutes — three bullet points, one per paragraph.
  3. Write with linking words: and, but, because, so, also, then, after that, finally.
  4. Check the -s on every he/she/it verb. This is where most marks are lost.
  5. Check capital letters, full stops, and that you answered all the points.

Model — "Describe your daily routine" (68 words)
I get up at half past six every morning. First I have a shower and get dressed, then I have breakfast with my family. I go to school by bus at seven o'clock, because my school is far from my house. In the afternoon I do my homework and I play football with my friends. I never go to bed late because I am always tired!

Model — "Write an email about your holiday" (74 words)
Hi Sam,
I am on holiday in Brazil with my family. We travel by boat every day because there are no roads here. My father takes hundreds of photos and my sister goes swimming every afternoon. Our hotel is small but the beach is amazing. Yesterday we bought some souvenirs and everybody was happy.
What about you? Does your family go anywhere in July?
Write soon,
Leo
🗣️ Speaking — never answer with one word

rows.en: What do you do in your free time?
"In my free time I play football and I go swimming, because I love sport."
"In my bedroom there is a bed, a wardrobe and a desk. My lamp is on the bedside table, next to my bed."
What clothes do you wear at school?
"I usually wear a blue shirt, grey trousers and black shoes. At the weekend I wear jeans and a hoodie."
How do you travel to school?
"I travel by bus. I get on at eight o'clock and I get off in front of the school."
Where do you go on holiday?
"We usually go on holiday in July. We stay at a hotel and we go sightseeing every day."

html.en: Golden speaking rule: answer + because + one extra detail. Two sentences is always better than one word.
